rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi understands the abundant water as plentiful.
rows.anchor: المنهمر الكثير , قاله السدي ، قال الشاعر : أعيني جودا

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad takes the water as pouring and cascading.
rows.anchor: المنصب المتدفق , قاله المبرد ، ومنه قول امرىء القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives two readings of heaven's opening: opening its gates and widening its passages, or the Milky Way, the seam of heaven, as Ali says.
rows.anchor: أنه فتح رتاجها وسعة مسالكها

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali identifies the opening as the Milky Way, a seam in heaven from which water poured.
rows.anchor: أنها المجرة وهي شرج السماء ومنها فتحت بماء منهمر , قاله علي

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba says the waters of heaven and earth met in a measured amount, neither exceeding the other.
rows.anchor: لم يزد أحدهما على الآخر , حكاه , ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reads the measure as a decree that the disbelievers would drown.
rows.anchor: قدر بمعنى قضي عليهم , قاله قتادة , وقدر لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vessel made of boards and fastenings is Noah's ship.
rows.anchor: دسر } أي السفينة , وفي الدسر أربعة أقاويل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the duser as crosspieces binding the ship's breadth.
rows.anchor: المعاريض التي يشد بها عرض السفينة ، قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن جبير وابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd take the duser as nails that fastened the ship together.
rows.anchor: دسرت بها السفينة ، أي شدت ، قاله ابن جبير وابن زيد

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says the duser is the ship's prow, which pushes against the water.
rows.anchor: صدر السفينة الذي يضرب الموج , قاله عكرمة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak takes the duser as the ship's two ends and its base.
rows.anchor: أنها طرفاها ، وأصلها ، قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Running under God's eyes means running within His sight.
rows.anchor: أحدها : بمرأى منا . الثاني : بأمرنا

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak explains God's eyes as His command.
rows.anchor: بأمرنا ، قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation has the ship under the eyes of angels assigned to guard it.
rows.anchor: بأعين أوليائنا من الملائكة الموكلين بحفظها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the eyes as the springs God caused to follow, linking the phrase to the bursting of earth's springs in 54:12.
rows.anchor: الرابع : بأعين الماء التي أتبعناها في قوله : { وفجرنا الأرض عيونا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further account says the ship ran between the waters of earth and heaven, which God had made cover it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنها تجري بين ماء الأرض والسماء ، وقد كان غطاها عن أمر الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd understand the recompense as payment for the people's disbelief in God.
rows.anchor: لكفرهم بالله ، قاله مجاهد ، وابن زيد

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the ship was recompense for the people's rejection of Noah.
rows.anchor: قاله السدي . الثالث : مكافأة لنوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ship may also be recompense for Noah, whom his people had disbelieved.
rows.anchor: مكافأة لنوح حين كفره قومه أن حمل ذات ألواح ودسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The thing left as a sign is understood either as the drowning or as the ship.
rows.anchor: أحدها : الغرق . الثاني : السفينة روى سعيد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: A report from Qatada says God preserved the ship at Baqird in the Jazira as a sign, where early Muslims saw it.
rows.anchor: روى سعيد عن قتادة أن الله أبقاها بباقردي من أرض الجزيرة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd reads the call for a reminder as asking whether anyone will take heed.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن زيد . الثاني : فهل من طالب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada understands it as asking whether anyone seeks good and is helped toward it.
rows.anchor: فهل من طالب خير فيعان عليه , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: محمد بن كعب
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b reads it as asking whether anyone will be restrained from disobeying God.
rows.anchor: فهل من مزدجر عن معاصي الله , قاله محمد بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making the Quran easy for remembrance means making its recitation accessible to speakers of every language; al-Mawardi calls this one of its miracles.
rows.anchor: لأن الأعجمي قد يقرأه ويتلوه كالعربي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil explains the phrase as making the Quran's knowledge and the derivation of its meanings easy.
rows.anchor: سهلنا علم ما فيه واستنباط معانيه ، قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra says God made the Quran easy to memorize, making it the easiest book to retain.
rows.anchor: هو كتاب الله ، قاله الفراء .

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report from Abu Hurayra says Quraysh disputed predestination with the Prophet, and this verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: روى إسماعيل بن زياد عن محمد بن عباد عن أبي هريرة أن مشركي قريش

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr says God created everything according to His will, without addition or shortfall.
rows.anchor: على قدر ما أردنا من غير زيادة ولا نقصان ، قاله ابن بحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes qadar as a prior decree and an unavoidable judgment, supported by a rajaz line.
rows.anchor: بحكم سابق وقضاء محتوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever God wills is commanded once; it needs no repetition and occurs as quickly as the blink of an eye, without delay.
rows.anchor: أمرنا به مرة واحدة ولم نحتج فيه إلى ثانية , فيكون ذلك الشيء مع أمرنا به كلمح البصر

rows.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وابن زيد
rows.claim: Hasan, Ikrima, and Ibn Zayd say every small and great deed is written down.
rows.anchor: أن المستطر المكتوب , قاله الحسن وعكرمة وابن زيد , لأنه مسطور

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says every deed is preserved.
rows.anchor: أنه المحفوظ , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj takes the river as rivers of water, wine, honey, and milk.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن جريج . الثاني : أن النهر الضياء

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq understands the river as radiance and light, related to daytime.
rows.anchor: أن النهر الضياء والنور , ومنه النهار , قاله محمد بن إسحاق

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: Qutrub reads it as spacious living and abundant bliss, like the breadth suggested by a river's name.
rows.anchor: قاله قطرب . { في مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A seat of truth is a place without idle talk or sin.
rows.anchor: مقعد حق لا لغو فيه ولا تأثيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is the true seat God promised His allies.
rows.anchor: مقعد صدق لله وعد أولياءه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Malik can mean the one who deserves kingship, while al-mulk denotes rule; al-Muqtadir means the powerful.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل ثالثا : أن المليك مستحق الملك , والملك القائم بالملك والمقتدر بمعنى القادر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God powerful magnifies the rank of the people with Him.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : لتعظيم شأن من عنده من المتقين لأنهم عند المقتدر أعظم قدرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also assures the people of Paradise that God can preserve His blessings and make them last.
rows.anchor: الثاني : ليعلموا أنه قادر على حفظ ما أنعم به عليهم ودوامه لهم

rows.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وجابر
rows.claim: Hasan, Ikrima, and Jabir classify all of Surat al-Rahman as Meccan.
rows.anchor: سورة الرحمن مكية كلها في قول الحسن ، وعكرمة ، وجابر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the sura is Meccan except for the verse about all in the heavens and earth asking of God.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : إلا آية ، وهي قوله تعالى : ^ ( يسأله من في السموات والأرض ) ^ الآية

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Masud and Muqatil classify all of Surat al-Rahman as Medinan.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود ، ومقاتل : هي مدنية كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min dunihima can mean two gardens nearer to the first pair, or two gardens lower in rank.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أي أقرب منهما جنتان . الثاني : أي دون صفتهما جنتان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says all four gardens belong to those who fear their Lord: the first pair has palms and trees, the latter pair crops and spreading plants.
rows.anchor: أن الجنات الأربع لمن خاف مقام ربه , قال ابن عباس : فيكون في الأوليين النخل والشجر

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd assigns the first pair, made of gold, to those brought near and the latter pair, made of silver, to the people of the right.
rows.anchor: أن الأوليين من ذهب للمقربين , والأخريين من ورق لأصحاب اليمين , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan assigns the first pair to the foremost and the latter pair to their followers.
rows.anchor: أن الأوليين للسابقين , والأخريين للتابعين , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil identifies the first pair as the Garden of Eden and the Garden of Bliss, and the latter pair as al-Firdaws and the Garden of Refuge; each pair includes many gardens.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل : الجنتان الأوليان جنة عدن وجنة النعيم والأخريان جنة الفردوس وجنة المأوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi also suggests the lower gardens may belong to the first pair's followers because of their lesser station, with one for houris and one for immortal youths.
rows.anchor: أن يكون من دونهما جنتان لأتباعه , لقصور منزلتهم عن منزلته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the gardens are green.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أي خضراوان , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says they are black, deriving the term from al-dahma, blackness; dark horses are likewise called adham.
rows.anchor: مسودتان , قاله مجاهد , مأخوذ من الدهمة وهي السواد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada describes the gardens as verdant and lush.
rows.anchor: [ خضروان من الري ] ناعمتان , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the two gushing springs are full and never cease.
rows.anchor: ممتلئتان لا تنقطعان , قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra reads the springs as flowing.
rows.anchor: جاريتان , قاله الفراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The springs may be spurting; the first pair's springs are described as flowing, which is stronger than spurting.
rows.anchor: الثالث : فوارتان , وذكر في الجنتين الأوليين عينين تجريان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the springs gush water.
rows.anchor: بالماء , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas says the springs gush musk and ambergris.
rows.anchor: بالمسك والعنبر , قاله أنس

rows.speaker: الحسن والكلبي
rows.claim: Hasan and al-Kalbi say the springs gush goodness and blessing.
rows.anchor: بالخير والبركة ، قاله الحسن ، والكلبي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr says the springs gush varieties of fruit.
rows.anchor: بأنواع الفاكهة , قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi notes two readings of khayrat, one with a lightened pronunciation, before beginning to list interpretations of its meaning.
rows.anchor: إحداهما بالتخفيف ، وفي المراد بها قولان

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: For the preceding phrase about loss, Ikrima gives the sense of being passionately attached, citing Namir ibn Tawlab's poetry.
rows.anchor: الثاني : مولع بنا , قاله عكرمة , ومنه قول النمر بن تولب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid gives the preceding phrase the sense of being deprived of one's share, citing poetry about two days of hardship.
rows.anchor: الثالث : محرومون من الحظ , قاله مجاهد , ومنه قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire people kindle is extracted with a fire drill from wood, iron, or stone.
rows.anchor: أي تستخرجون بزنادكم من شجر أو حديد أو حجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To originate the fire's tree means to bring forth its root; God is the one who produces it.
rows.anchor: أي أخذتم أصلها . { أم نحن المنشئون } يعني المحدثون

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the fire is a reminder of the greater fire of the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: قاله قتادة . الثاني : تبصرة للناس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid understands the fire as a means of seeing through darkness.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد . { ومتاعا للمقوين } فيه خمسة أقاويل

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the fire is a benefit for travelers; al-Farra explains that travelers are called al-muqwīn when they camp in barren land.
rows.anchor: منفعة للمسافرين قاله الضحاك ، قال الفراء : إنما يقال للمسافرين إذا نزلوا القي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the fire benefits anyone who enjoys it, whether settled or traveling.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد . الثالث : للجائعين

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the fire serves hungry people when they prepare food.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن زيد . الرابع : الضعفاء والمساكين

rows.speaker: ابن عيسى
rows.claim: Ibn Isa takes al-muqwīn as the weak and poor, deriving it from an empty, uninhabited home.
rows.anchor: حكاه ابن عيسى . والعرب تقول قد أقوى الرجل إذا ذهب ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic usage also calls a person aqwā when he has lost his wealth; al-Nabigha's verse depicts travelers left with only a fire drill and kindling.
rows.anchor: والعرب تقول قد أقوى الرجل إذا ذهب ماله , قال النابغة : يقوى بها الركب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poor emigrants are Muslims who left their homes for Medina to escape their people's harm and support the Prophet; they were foremost in Islam.
rows.anchor: فهم المقدمون في الإسلام على جميع أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's favor and good pleasure can mean worldly provision and otherworldly reward.
rows.anchor: يعني فضلا من عطاء الله في الدنيا , ورضوانا من ثوابه في الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, favor means sufficiency and good pleasure means contentment.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل وجها ثانيا : أن الفضل الكفاية , والرضوان القناعة

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: In a sermon at al-Jabiya, Umar directed questions on inheritance to Zayd, jurisprudence to Muadh, and wealth to himself as God's treasurer; he said he would begin distributing to the Prophet's wives and then the first emigrants who left Mecca's homes and wealth.
rows.anchor: وروى علي بن رباح اللخمي أن عمر بن الخطاب خطب بالجابية فقال : من أراد أن يسأل عن الفرائض

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reports that the emigrants chose God and His Messenger despite hunger and exposure: one tied a stone to his belly, and another wintered in a pit without a covering.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : لأنهم اختاروا الله ورسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم على ما كانت من شدة , حتى ذكر لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One syntactic reading uses fronting and postponement: they settled the abode before the emigrants and had embraced faith.
rows.anchor: ويكون على التقديم والتأخير ومعناه تبوءوا الدار من قبلهم والإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the surface reading, they had settled the abode and faith before the emigrants came, welcoming and supporting them with homes and wealth.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن الكلام على ظاهره ومعناه أنهم تبوءوا الدار والإيمان قبل الهجرة إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not finding need in their hearts may mean having no jealousy or envy over the emigrants' preference and closeness.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : غيرة وحسدا على ما قدموا به من تفضيل وتقريب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan specifies that they did not envy the emigrants for the property of the spoils and other wealth allotted to them.
rows.anchor: الثاني : يعني حسدا على ما خصوا به من مال الفيء وغيره فلا يحسدونهم عليه , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They put the emigrants first even when they themselves faced poverty and need.
rows.anchor: يعني يفضلونهم ويقدمونهم على أنفسهم ولو كان بهم فاقة وحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited verse uses khisasa for poverty and need; the poem says the sickly prosper when spring arrives.
rows.anchor: أما الربيع إذا تكون خصاصة

rows.speaker: مجاهد وابن حيان
rows.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Hayyan say the Ansar preferred the emigrants in the fay and booty allotted to them, despite their own need.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد , وابن حيان .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed report says that after the Prophet allocated Banu al-Nadir's fay and Qurayza's spoils to the emigrants, the Ansar offered their own property and chose that the emigrants receive the fay; the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قسم على المهاجرين ما أفاء الله من النضير ونفل من قريظة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Ansar preferred the emigrants by giving them their own wealth and sharing it with them.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنهم آثروا المهاجرين بأموالهم وواسوهم بها . روى ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: In Ibn Zayd's report, the Ansar offered divided estates; the Prophet proposed caring for the emigrants, who could not work, and sharing dates from Banu al-Nadir's palms, and they agreed.
rows.anchor: روى ابن زيد أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن جريج وطاووس
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Tawus define soul's avarice as wanting wealth in other people's hands for oneself without being content.
rows.anchor: أن يشح بما في أيدي الناس يحب أن يكون له ولا يقنع , قاله ابن جريج وطاووس

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr interprets it as withholding zakat.
rows.anchor: أنه منع الزكاة ، قاله ابن جبير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says it is the soul's desire.
rows.anchor: يعني هوى نفسه ، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud defines the Quranic avarice as acquiring forbidden wealth, specifically consuming another person's property unjustly.
rows.anchor: إنما الشح الذي ذكره الله في القرآن أن تأكل مال أخيك ظلما ولكن ذلك البخل

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Al-Aswad reports a man feared damnation because he was too stingy to give; Ibn Masud answered that ordinary miserliness is not the Quranic avarice, which is wrongful appropriation.
rows.anchor: روى الأسود عن ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata interprets it as withholding expenditure.
rows.anchor: أنه الإمساك عن النفقة , قاله عطاء

rows.speaker: ابن عيينة
rows.claim: Ibn Uyayna interprets it as injustice.
rows.anchor: أنه الظلم , قاله ابن عيينة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan understands it as acting on one's desire to disobey God.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد العمل بمعاصي الله , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says it means abandoning obligations and violating prohibitions.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد ترك الفرائض وانتهاك المحارم , قاله الليث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says shuhh and bukhl mean the same thing.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أن معناهما واحد

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud distinguishes them: shuhh is taking wealth without right, while bukhl is withholding what is due.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن مسعود . الثاني : أن الشح بما في يدي غيره

rows.speaker: طاووس
rows.claim: Tawus distinguishes them by ownership: shuhh covets another's property, while bukhl concerns one's own.
rows.anchor: قاله طاووس . { والذين جاءوا من بعدهم يقولون ربنا }

rows.speaker: السدي والكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and al-Kalbi identify those who came later as people who emigrated after the first emigrants.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم الذين هاجروا بعد ذلك , قاله السدي والكلبي

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil identifies them as the Successors after the Companions and all later generations until the end of the world.
rows.anchor: قاله مقاتل . وروى مصعب بن سعد

rows.speaker: مصعب بن سعد
rows.claim: Musab ibn Sad says humanity has three generations: two have passed and the third remains; he urges his audience to belong to that remaining generation.
rows.anchor: وروى مصعب بن سعد قال : الناس على ثلاثة منازل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says later believers are to seek forgiveness for everyone in the community before them, including believing People of the Book.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنهم أمروا أن يستغفروا لمن سبق من هذه الأمة ومن مؤمني أهل الكتاب

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha said they were ordered to seek forgiveness for those before them but instead cursed them.
rows.anchor: قالت عائشة : فأمروا أن يستغفروا لهم فسبوهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation says the prayer is for the earliest emigrants and the Ansar.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنهم أمروا أن يستغفروا للسابقين الأولين من المهاجرين والأنصار

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil interprets rancor as deceit or guile.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : الغش , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Amash interprets rancor as enmity.
rows.anchor: الثاني : العداوة , قاله الأعمش

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb takes al-Quddus to mean the pure one, supported by a rajaz line.
rows.anchor: أنه الطاهر , قاله وهب

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj derives al-Quddus from the angels' act of sanctifying God.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنه اسم مشتق من تقديس الملائكة , قاله ابن جريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the angels glorify God with the words Subbuh Quddus, Lord of the angels and the Spirit.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أن من تسبيح الملائكة سبوح قدوس رب الملائكة والروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Quddus can mean the one free of blemishes, with the meaning tied to the angels' sanctifying praise.
rows.anchor: الرابع : معناه المنزه عن القبائح لاشتقاقه من تقديس الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Salam is one of God's names, like al-Quddus.
rows.anchor: وأما { السلام } فهو من أسمائه تعالى كالقدوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One derivation links al-Salam to God's safety and permanence; a poem by Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من سلامته وبقائه , فإذا وصف المخلوق بمثله قيل سالم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas derives al-Salam from God's keeping His servants safe from injustice.
rows.anchor: أنه مأخوذ من سلامة عباده من ظلمه , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mumin means the one who secures His allies from punishment.
rows.anchor: الذي يؤمن أولياءه من عذابه

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says al-Mumin means the one who confirms His creatures in His promise.
rows.anchor: وهو معنى قول ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Bahr says al-Mumin is the one who calls people to faith.
rows.anchor: أنه الداعي إلى الإيمان , قاله ابن بحر

rows.speaker: قتادة والمفضل
rows.claim: Qatada and al-Mufaddal say al-Muhaymin witnesses His creatures' deeds and holds Himself responsible for their reward.
rows.anchor: قاله قتادة , والمفضل , وأنشد قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak interprets al-Muhaymin as the trustworthy one.
rows.anchor: الأمين ، قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd interprets al-Muhaymin as the confirmer.
rows.anchor: المصدق ، قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن كامل
rows.claim: Ibn Kamil says al-Muhaymin means the protector.
rows.anchor: أنه الحافظ ، حكاه ابن كامل

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: A report says Umar used hayminu to mean say amen, preserving the supplication in hope of its acceptance.
rows.anchor: وروي أن عمر بن الخطاب قال : إني داع فهيمنوا

rows.speaker: ابن تغلب
rows.claim: Ibn Taghlib interprets al-Muhaymin as the merciful one and cites Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt.
rows.anchor: حكاه ابن تغلب واستشهد بقول أمية بن أبي الصلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aziz means the overpowering one, either through inviolability or through vengeance.
rows.anchor: هو القاهر , وفيه وجهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Jabbar can mean lofty and immense in power and authority.
rows.anchor: معناه العالي العظيم الشأن في القدرة والسلطان

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra, Hasan, and Qatada say al-Jabbar is the one who compels His creatures as He wills.
rows.anchor: الذي جبر خلقه على ما شاء , قاله أبو هريرة , والحسن , وقتادة

rows.speaker: واصل بن عطاء
rows.claim: Wasil ibn Ata says al-Jabbar is the one who repairs His servants' poverty.
rows.anchor: أنه الذي يجبر فاقة عباده , قاله واصل بن عطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further explanation says all beneath God are humbled before Him.
rows.anchor: أنه الذي يذل له من دونه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says al-Mutakabbir is exalted above sins.
rows.anchor: المتكبر عن السيئات , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutakabbir can mean deserving greatness and exaltation; the attribute praises God but condemns creatures who claim it.
rows.anchor: والتكبر في صفات الله مدح , وفي صفات المخلوقين ذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutakabbir can also mean exalted above wronging His servants.
rows.anchor: المتكبر عن ظلم عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khaliq is the one who brings things into existence according to His will.
rows.anchor: أنه المحدث للأشياء على إرادته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, al-Khaliq is the one who determines things with wisdom.
rows.anchor: أنه المقدر لها بحكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bari may mean the one who distinguishes creatures, as in the expression meaning I separated myself from him.
rows.anchor: المميز للخلق , ومنه قوله : برئت منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may also mean the one who originates creation; a cited line supports that sense.
rows.anchor: المنشىء للخلق , ومنه قول الشاعر :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetry supports al-Bari as the one who brings creation into being.
rows.anchor: براك الله حين براه غيثا ويجري منك أنهارا عذابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Musawwir may mean shaping each creature according to God's will when it is first created.
rows.anchor: لتصوير الخلق على مشيئته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means giving each kind its own form and producing each generation in that established form; both readings demonstrate God's power.
rows.anchor: وعلى الوجه الثاني يكون محمولا على ما استقر من صور الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is moving humans and animals through successive forms, from sperm to clot to flesh and finally old age, as al-Nabigha's line illustrates.
rows.anchor: ثم مضغة إلى أن يصير شيخا هرما , كما قال النابغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All God's names are beautiful because they derive from His beautiful attributes.
rows.anchor: أن جميع أسمائه حسنى لاشتقاقه من صفاته الحسنى

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says the phrase means God has the highest exemplars or qualities.
rows.anchor: أن له الأمثال العليا , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surat al-Mumtahana is Medinan according to all authorities cited.
rows.anchor: سورة الممتحنة مدنية في قول الجميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unlettered people among whom the Messenger was sent are the Arabs.
rows.anchor: يعني في العرب , وفي تسميتهم أميين قولان

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Arabs are called unlettered because no book was sent down to them.
rows.anchor: لأنه لم ينزل عليهم كتاب , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they are called unlettered because they did not write and had no scribe among them.
rows.anchor: لأنهم لم يكونوا يكتبون ولا كان فيهم كاتب , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view limits the unlettered people here to Quraysh, who did not write until some learned from the people of al-Hira late in the pre-Islamic period.
rows.anchor: أنهم قريش خاصة لأنها لم تكن تكتب حتى تعلم بعضها في آخر الجاهلية من أهل الحيرة

rows.speaker: المفضل
rows.claim: Al-Mufaddal says the term includes all Arabs because they had no scripture and only a few could write.
rows.anchor: أنهم جميع العرب لأنه لم يكن لهم كتاب ولا كتب منهم إلا قليل , قاله المفضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sending an unlettered prophet fulfilled the earlier prophets' glad tidings.
rows.anchor: لموافقته ما تقدمت بشارة الأنبياء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His state resembled theirs, making them more likely to accept him.
rows.anchor: حالِه لأحوالهم , فيكون أقرب إلى موافقتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His being unlettered also removed suspicion that he had learned the books and wisdom he recited from texts he had read.
rows.anchor: لينتفي عنه سوء الظن في تعلمه ما دعا إليه من الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs he recites to them are the Quran.
rows.anchor: يعني القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says he purifies them by making their hearts pure through faith.
rows.anchor: أزكياء القلوب بالإيمان , وهو معنى قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن جريج ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj and Muqatil say he purifies them from disbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: يطهرهم من الكفر والذنوب ، قاله ابن جريج ومقاتل

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi interprets purification as taking the zakat of their deeds.
rows.anchor: الثالث : يأخذ زكاة أعمالهم ، قاله السدي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the Book is the Quran.
rows.anchor: أنه القرآن ، قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Book is writing with a pen, which spread among Arabs through the religious command to record things in writing.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس ، لأن الخط إنما فشا في العرب بالشرع

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Ishaq says it is knowledge of good and evil through the Book, so people do good and refrain from evil.
rows.anchor: معرفة الخير والشر كما يعرفونه بالكتاب ليفعلوا الخير ويكفوا عن الشر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan interprets wisdom as the Sunna.
rows.anchor: أن الحكمة السنة ، قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik ibn Anas interprets wisdom as understanding jurisprudence in religion.
rows.anchor: أنه الفقه في الدين , وهو قول مالك بن أنس

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Amash says wisdom is understanding and taking admonition.
rows.anchor: أنه الفهم والاتعاظ , قاله الأعمش

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the later people as Muslims who came after the Companions.
rows.anchor: أنهم المسلمون بعد الصحابة , قاله ابن زيد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies them as non-Arabs who follow the Arabs; a report of the Prophet's dream uses dark sheep followed by pale sheep as an image for them.
rows.anchor: قاله الضحاك وقد روي عن النبي

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: In the dream report, Abu Bakr interprets the dark sheep as Arabs and the pale sheep as non-Arabs; the Prophet says the angel interpreted it that way.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو بكر : يا رسول الله تلك العرب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the later people are kings who are sons of non-Arabs.
rows.anchor: أنهم الملوك أبناء الأعاجم , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possibility is that the later people are children after men, or women after men.
rows.anchor: أنهم الأطفال بعد الرجال . ويحتمل خامسا : أنهم النساء بعد الرجال

words: ذَٰلِكَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Maqatil says God's bounty here is prophethood, which He specially gave His Messenger.
rows.anchor: أنها النبوة التي خص الله بها رسوله هي فضل الله يؤتيه من يشاء

words: ذَٰلِكَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies God's bounty as Islam, which God gave to whomever He willed.
rows.anchor: الإسلام الذي آتاه الله من شاء من عباده , قاله الكلبي

words: ذَٰلِكَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Abu Salih reports that the wealthy gained rewards through alms, so the Prophet taught the poor to glorify, praise, and magnify God; when the wealthy did the same, the Prophet said this is God's bounty given as He wills.
rows.anchor: ذهب أهل الدثور بالأجور ، فأمر ذوي الفاقة بالتسبيح والتحميد والتكبير

words: ذَٰلِكَ فَضْلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤْتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi also suggests God's bounty is people submitting to Muhammad's truth, entering his religion, and supporting him.
rows.anchor: انقياد الناس إلى تصديقه صلى الله عليه وسلم ودخولهم في دينه ونصرته
